passages.text: Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying, “Son of man, you are living in a rebellious house. They have eyes to see but do not see, and ears to hear but do not hear, for they are a rebellious house.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to me.
He said these words to me.
He called me “son of man.”
I live among a rebellious people.
These people belong to a rebellious house.
They have eyes.
They do not see with their eyes.
They have ears.
They do not hear with their ears.
They are a rebellious house.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־ יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃ בֶּן־ אָדָ֕ם בְּת֥וֹךְ בֵּית־ הַמֶּ֖רִי אַתָּ֣ה יֹשֵׁ֑ב אֲשֶׁ֣ר עֵינַיִם֩ לָהֶ֨ם לִרְא֜וֹת וְלֹ֣א רָא֗וּ אָזְנַ֨יִם לָהֶ֤ם לִשְׁמֹ֙עַ֙ וְלֹ֣א שָׁמֵ֔עוּ כִּ֛י בֵּ֥ית מְרִ֖י הֵֽם׃

passages.text: Therefore, son of man, pack your bags for exile. In broad daylight, set out from your place and go to another as they watch. Perhaps they will understand, though they are a rebellious house.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel.
Ezekiel was a prophet.
God called Ezekiel "son of man."
God told Ezekiel to pack his belongings for exile.
God told Ezekiel to do this while the people watched.
God told Ezekiel to leave his home during the day.
God told Ezekiel to go to another place as the people watched.
God said the people were rebellious.
God said maybe the people would understand.
passages.original: וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן־ אָדָ֗ם עֲשֵׂ֤ה לְךָ֙ כְּלֵ֣י גוֹלָ֔ה וּגְלֵ֥ה יוֹמָ֖ם לְעֵֽינֵיהֶ֑ם וְגָלִ֨יתָ מִמְּקוֹמְךָ֜ אֶל־ מָק֤וֹם אַחֵר֙ לְעֵ֣ינֵיהֶ֔ם אוּלַ֣י יִרְא֔וּ כִּ֛י בֵּ֥ית מְרִ֖י הֵֽמָּה׃

passages.text: Bring out your baggage for exile by day, as they watch. Then in the evening, as they watch, go out like those who go into exile.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel.
Ezekiel was a prophet.
God told Ezekiel to act as a sign for Israel.
God said, “Bring out your baggage for exile during the day.
Let the people watch you.
In the evening, go out as they watch.
Go out like people who are going into exile.”
passages.original: וְהוֹצֵאתָ֨ כֵלֶ֜יךָ כִּכְלֵ֥י גוֹלָ֛ה יוֹמָ֖ם לְעֵֽינֵיהֶ֑ם וְאַתָּ֗ה תֵּצֵ֤א בָעֶ֙רֶב֙ לְעֵ֣ינֵיהֶ֔ם כְּמוֹצָאֵ֖י גּוֹלָֽה׃

passages.text: As they watch, dig through the wall and carry your belongings out through it.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel.
God called Ezekiel "son of man."
God told Ezekiel to act as a sign for Israel.
Israel was a rebellious people.
God commanded Ezekiel to dig through the wall.
Ezekiel must do this while the people watch.
Ezekiel must carry his belongings out through the hole in the wall.
passages.original: לְעֵינֵיהֶ֖ם חֲתָר־ לְךָ֣ בַקִּ֑יר וְהוֹצֵאתָ֖ בּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: And as they watch, lift your bags to your shoulder and take them out at dusk; cover your face so that you cannot see the land. For I have made you a sign to the house of Israel.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel.
God told Ezekiel to act as a sign for Israel.
God told Ezekiel to do this while the people watched him.
God told Ezekiel to lift his bags onto his shoulder.
God told Ezekiel to carry his bags out at dusk.
God told Ezekiel to cover his face.
God told Ezekiel not to look at the land.
God said, “I have made you a sign to the house of Israel.”
passages.original: לְעֵ֨ינֵיהֶ֜ם עַל־ כָּתֵ֤ף תִּשָּׂא֙ בָּעֲלָטָ֣ה תוֹצִ֔יא פָּנֶ֣יךָ תְכַסֶּ֔ה וְלֹ֥א תִרְאֶ֖ה אֶת־ הָאָ֑רֶץ כִּֽי־ מוֹפֵ֥ת נְתַתִּ֖יךָ לְבֵ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: So I did as I was commanded. I brought out my bags for exile by day, and in the evening I dug through the wall by hand. I took my belongings out at dusk, carrying them on my shoulder as they watched.
passages.sermon:
God commanded me to act as a sign to Israel.
I obeyed God’s command.
During the day, I took out my bags.
These bags were like the bags of an exile.
In the evening, I dug through the wall with my hand.
At dusk, I took out my belongings.
I carried them on my shoulder.
The people watched me do this.
passages.original: וָאַ֣עַשׂ כֵּן֮ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר צֻוֵּיתִי֒ כֵּ֠לַי הוֹצֵ֜אתִי כִּכְלֵ֤י גוֹלָה֙ יוֹמָ֔ם וּבָעֶ֛רֶב חָתַֽרְתִּי־ לִ֥י בַקִּ֖יר בְּיָ֑ד בָּעֲלָטָ֥ה הוֹצֵ֛אתִי עַל־ כָּתֵ֥ף נָשָׂ֖אתִי לְעֵינֵיהֶֽם׃פ

passages.text: And in the morning the word of the LORD came to me, saying, “Son of man, hasn’t the rebellious house of Israel asked you, ‘What are you doing?’
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to me in the morning.
He gave me a message.
He called me “son of man.”
The house of Israel is rebellious.
They asked me a question.
They said, “What are you doing?”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֧י דְבַר־ יְהוָ֛ה אֵלַ֖י בַּבֹּ֥קֶר לֵאמֹֽר׃ בֶּן־ אָדָ֕ם הֲלֹ֨א אָמְר֥וּ אֵלֶ֛יךָ בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֑רִי מָ֖ה אַתָּ֥ה עֹשֶֽׂה׃

passages.text: Tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘This burden concerns the prince in Jerusalem and all the house of Israel who are there.’
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD spoke.
He gave a message.
This message is for the prince in Jerusalem.
This message is also for all the people of Israel who live there.
The Lord GOD says this message is a burden for them.
passages.original: אֱמֹ֣ר אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֑ה הַנָּשִׂ֞יא הַמַּשָּׂ֤א הַזֶּה֙ בִּיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וְכָל־ בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֲשֶׁר־ הֵ֥מָּה בְתוֹכָֽם׃

passages.text: You are to say, ‘I am a sign to you.’ Just as it happened here, so will it be done to them; they will go into exile as captives.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel.
God called Ezekiel "son of man."
God told Ezekiel to speak to Israel.
Israel is a rebellious people.
God told Ezekiel to say, "I am a sign to you."
God used Ezekiel as an example for Israel.
What happened to Ezekiel is a sign for Israel.
The same thing will happen to the people of Israel.
The people of Israel will go into exile.
They will become captives.
passages.original: אֱמֹ֖ר אֲנִ֣י מֽוֹפֶתְכֶ֑ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֗יתִי כֵּ֚ן יֵעָשֶׂ֣ה לָהֶ֔ם בַּגּוֹלָ֥ה בַשְּׁבִ֖י יֵלֵֽכוּ׃

passages.text: And at dusk the prince among them will lift his bags to his shoulder and go out. They will dig through the wall to bring him out. He will cover his face so he cannot see the land.
passages.sermon:
The prince lives among the people in Jerusalem.
He will act at dusk.
He will lift his bags onto his shoulder.
He will go out in the darkness.
People will dig through the wall to bring him out.
He will cover his face.
He will not see the land.
passages.original: וְהַנָּשִׂ֨יא אֲשֶׁר־ בְּתוֹכָ֜ם אֶל־ כָּתֵ֤ף יִשָּׂא֙ בָּעֲלָטָ֣ה וְיֵצֵ֔א בַּקִּ֥יר יַחְתְּר֖וּ לְה֣וֹצִיא ב֑וֹ פָּנָ֣יו יְכַסֶּ֔ה יַ֗עַן אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹא־ יִרְאֶ֥ה לַעַ֛יִן ה֖וּא אֶת־ הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: But I will spread My net over him, and he will be caught in My snare. I will bring him to Babylon, the land of the Chaldeans; yet he will not see it, and there he will die.
passages.sermon:
God speaks these words.
God says, “I will spread my net over the prince.
He will be caught in my snare.
I will bring him to Babylon.
Babylon is the land of the Chaldeans.
He will not see that land.
He will die there.”
passages.original: וּפָרַשְׂתִּ֤י אֶת־ רִשְׁתִּי֙ עָלָ֔יו וְנִתְפַּ֖שׂ בִּמְצֽוּדָתִ֑י וְהֵבֵאתִ֨י אֹת֤וֹ בָבֶ֙לָה֙ אֶ֣רֶץ כַּשְׂדִּ֔ים וְאוֹתָ֥הּ לֹֽא־ יִרְאֶ֖ה וְשָׁ֥ם יָמֽוּת׃

passages.text: And I will scatter to every wind all the attendants around him and all his troops, and I will draw a sword to chase after them.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about the prince and his people.
God will scatter all the attendants who are around the prince.
God will scatter all his troops to every wind.
God will draw a sword.
God will chase after them with the sword.
passages.original: וְכֹל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר סְבִיבֹתָ֥יו עֶזְרֹה וְכָל־ אֲגַפָּ֖יו אֱזָרֶ֣ה לְכָל־ ר֑וּחַ וְחֶ֖רֶב אָרִ֥יק אַחֲרֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: And they will know that I am the LORD, when I disperse them among the nations and scatter them throughout the countries.
passages.sermon:
God is the LORD.
God will disperse the people among the nations.
God will scatter the people throughout the countries.
Then the people will know that God is the LORD.
passages.original: וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי־ אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֑ה בַּהֲפִיצִ֤י אוֹתָם֙ בַּגּוֹיִ֔ם וְזֵרִיתִ֥י אוֹתָ֖ם בָּאֲרָצֽוֹת׃

passages.text: But I will spare a few of them from sword and famine and plague, so that in the nations to which they go, they can recount all their abominations. Then they will know that I am the LORD.”
passages.sermon:
God speaks about the people of Israel.
God says He will spare a small number of them.
He will save them from the sword.
He will save them from famine.
He will save them from plague.
God will scatter these survivors among the nations.
These people will tell about all their abominations.
They will speak about their sins in the places where they go.
Then the people will know that God is the LORD.
passages.original: וְהוֹתַרְתִּ֤י מֵהֶם֙ אַנְשֵׁ֣י מִסְפָּ֔ר מֵחֶ֖רֶב מֵרָעָ֣ב וּמִדָּ֑בֶר לְמַ֨עַן יְסַפְּר֜וּ אֶת־ כָּל־ תּוֹעֲבֽוֹתֵיהֶ֗ם בַּגּוֹיִם֙ אֲשֶׁר־ בָּ֣אוּ שָׁ֔ם וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי־ אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃פ

passages.text: Moreover, the word of the LORD came to me, saying, “Son of man, eat your bread with trembling, and drink your water with quivering and anxiety.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to me.
He said these words to me.
He called me "Son of man."
He told me to eat my bread with trembling.
He told me to drink my water with quivering and anxiety.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־ יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃ בֶּן־ אָדָ֕ם לַחְמְךָ֖ בְּרַ֣עַשׁ תֹּאכֵ֑ל וּמֵימֶ֕יךָ בְּרָגְזָ֥ה וּבִדְאָגָ֖ה תִּשְׁתֶּֽה׃

passages.text: Then tell the people of the land that this is what the Lord GOD says about those living in Jerusalem and in the land of Israel: ‘They will eat their bread with anxiety and drink their water in dread, for their land will be stripped of everything in it because of the violence of all who dwell in it.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks to the people of the land.
He speaks about those who live in Jerusalem.
He speaks about those who live in the land of Israel.
They will eat their bread with anxiety.
They will drink their water in dread.
Their land will lose everything in it.
This will happen because of the violence of all who live there.
passages.original: וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֶל־ עַ֣ם הָאָ֡רֶץ כֹּֽה־ אָמַר֩ אֲדֹנָ֨י יְהוִ֜ה לְיוֹשְׁבֵ֤י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ אֶל־ אַדְמַ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לַחְמָם֙ בִּדְאָגָ֣ה יֹאכֵ֔לוּ וּמֵֽימֵיהֶ֖ם בְּשִׁמָּמ֣וֹן יִשְׁתּ֑וּ לְמַ֜עַן תֵּשַׁ֤ם אַרְצָהּ֙ מִמְּלֹאָ֔הּ מֵחֲמַ֖ס כָּֽל־ הַיֹּשְׁבִ֥ים בָּֽהּ׃

passages.text: The inhabited cities will be laid waste, and the land will become desolate. Then you will know that I am the LORD.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Ezekiel.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD said what would happen to the people.
The cities where people live will be destroyed.
The land will become empty and ruined.
You will know that I am the LORD.
passages.original: וְהֶעָרִ֤ים הַנּֽוֹשָׁבוֹת֙ תֶּחֱרַ֔בְנָה וְהָאָ֖רֶץ שְׁמָמָ֣ה תִֽהְיֶ֑ה וִֽידַעְתֶּ֖ם כִּֽי־ אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃פ

passages.text: Again the word of the LORD came to me, saying, “Son of man, what is this proverb that you have in the land of Israel: ‘The days go by, and every vision fails’?
passages.sermon:
The word of the LORD came to me again.
God spoke to me.
He called me "Son of man."
God asked me a question.
He said, "What is this proverb you have in the land of Israel?"
The people in Israel say this proverb.
They say, "The days go by."
They say, "Every vision fails."
passages.original: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־ יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃ בֶּן־ אָדָ֗ם מָֽה־ הַמָּשָׁ֤ל הַזֶּה֙ לָכֶ֔ם עַל־ אַדְמַ֥ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר יַֽאַרְכוּ֙ הַיָּמִ֔ים וְאָבַ֖ד כָּל־ חָזֽוֹן׃

passages.text: Therefore tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘I will put an end to this proverb, and in Israel they will no longer recite it.’ But say to them: ‘The days are at hand when every vision will be fulfilled.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks.
He says, "I will end this proverb."
Israel will not use this proverb anymore.
Tell the people this message.
The days are near.
Every vision will come true soon.
passages.original: לָכֵ֞ן אֱמֹ֣ר אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם כֹּֽה־ אָמַר֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ הִשְׁבַּ֙תִּי֙ אֶת־ הַמָּשָׁ֣ל הַזֶּ֔ה וְלֹֽא־ יִמְשְׁל֥וּ אֹת֛וֹ ע֖וֹד בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּ֚י אִם־ דַּבֵּ֣ר אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם קָֽרְבוּ֙ הַיָּמִ֔ים וּדְבַ֖ר כָּל־ חָזֽוֹן׃

passages.text: For there will be no more false visions or flattering divinations within the house of Israel, because I, the LORD, will speak whatever word I speak, and it will be fulfilled without delay. For in your days, O rebellious house, I will speak a message and bring it to pass, declares the Lord GOD.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is speaking to the house of Israel.
The LORD says there will be no more false visions in Israel.
There will be no more flattering divinations among the people.
I am the LORD.
When I speak a word, I will do what I say.
There will be no more delay.
You are a rebellious house.
In your days, I will speak a message.
I will make it happen, declares the Lord GOD.
passages.original: כִּ֠י לֹ֣א יִֽהְיֶ֥ה ע֛וֹד כָּל־ חֲז֥וֹן שָׁ֖וְא וּמִקְסַ֣ם חָלָ֑ק בְּת֖וֹךְ בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ כִּ֣י׀ אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֗ה אֲדַבֵּר֙ אֵת֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר אֲדַבֵּ֤ר דָּבָר֙ וְיֵ֣עָשֶׂ֔ה לֹ֥א תִמָּשֵׁ֖ךְ ע֑וֹד כִּ֣י בִֽימֵיכֶ֞ם בֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֗רִי אֲדַבֵּ֤ר דָּבָר֙ וַעֲשִׂיתִ֔יו נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃פ

passages.text: Furthermore, the word of the LORD came to me, saying, “Son of man, take note that the house of Israel is saying, ‘The vision that he sees is for many years from now; he prophesies about the distant future.’
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to me.
He said these words to me.
He called me "son of man."
The people of Israel are speaking.
They say this about the visions I see.
They say, "The vision he sees is for many years from now."
They say, "He prophesies about times that are far away."
passages.original: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־ יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃ בֶּן־ אָדָ֗ם הִנֵּ֤ה בֵֽית־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֹֽמְרִ֔ים הֶחָז֛וֹן אֲשֶׁר־ ה֥וּא חֹזֶ֖ה לְיָמִ֣ים רַבִּ֑ים וּלְעִתִּ֥ים רְחוֹק֖וֹת ה֥וּא נִבָּֽא׃

passages.text: Therefore tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘None of My words will be delayed any longer. The message I speak will be fulfilled, declares the Lord GOD.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks with authority.
He says, “None of My words will be delayed any longer.
Every message I speak will be fulfilled.
I, the Lord GOD, declare this.”
passages.original: לָכֵ֞ן אֱמֹ֣ר אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה לֹא־ תִמָּשֵׁ֥ךְ ע֖וֹד כָּל־ דְּבָרָ֑י אֲשֶׁ֨ר אֲדַבֵּ֤ר דָּבָר֙ וְיֵ֣עָשֶׂ֔ה נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃ס
